resources.string: Find apps that can steal your OTP codes, and shut them down.
These apps come from unknown sources and can read your verification codes or control your phone. Unless you are sure what they are, uninstall them now.
They can read important information or operate your phone. Fine if you turned it on yourself. Otherwise turn it off.
No app can read your SMS, notifications or screen. Check again after installing new apps.
Can read everything on screen, tap and type for you. The main tool scammers use to take over phones.
Can read the one-time codes your bank texts you.
Can read every notification, including OTP codes.
Can lock your phone and stop you from uninstalling it.
Can draw a fake login page on top of your bank app.
Can silently bring in more malicious apps.
Turn off Device admin first, otherwise the app cannot be uninstalled.
Banks and government agencies never ask you to turn on Accessibility or install an app from a link.
Only install apps from Google Play.
Never tell anyone your OTP code, not even someone claiming to be bank staff.
If you think money was taken, call your bank and the anti-fraud hotline immediately.
Installed from an app store or by your phone maker. Many normal apps need these. Tap to review.
They hold no dangerous access right now. If you don\'t recognise one, uninstall it.
Sees every OTP and password you type.
Can read call history, make or redirect calls, e.g. to fake bank hotlines.
A VPN from an unknown source can see what you do online.
Knows when you open your bank app, so a fake page can pop up at that moment.
A VPN is connected right now. Make sure it is one you set up yourself.
USB debugging is on. Turn it off unless you are a developer.
